stem: An older adult with atrial fibrillation develops sudden severe abdominal pain that is much greater than expected from the initial abdominal examination. Which condition is most concerning?
rationale: Acute mesenteric ischemia classically presents with sudden severe abdominal pain that may be out of proportion to early examination findings. Atrial fibrillation is an important embolic risk factor.
educational_objective: Recognize the classic presentation and embolic risk context of acute mesenteric ischemia.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_locator: Clinical presentation: severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam; embolic risk including atrial fibrillation
source_claim_supported: Sudden severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam in a patient with atrial fibrillation is concerning for acute mesenteric ischemia.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — acute vascular gastrointestinal emergency
correction_summary: Corrected the source mismatch and used the current StatPearls presentation/risk-factor description.
